court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
case_name: Amit Kumar vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

parties.respondent_defendant: State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko. And Others

facts_of_case: Petitioner filed a writ petition to quash the First Information Report No.1049/2019 against him under various IPC sections and Dowry Prohibition Act. The parties have arrived at a compromise.

legal_principles.principle: Criminal proceedings can be quashed by the court under its inherent power on the basis of mutual settlement.
legal_principles.held: The Apex Court considering the previous judgments of the Supreme Court has held that the criminal proceedings can be quashed by this Court under its inherent power on the basis of mutual settlement.
cited_cases: Jitendra Raghuvanshi and Ors. Vs. Babita Raghuvanshi and Ors., (2013) (4) ADJ 40

legal_principles.principle: Technicality should not be allowed to stand in the way of quashing criminal proceeding.
legal_principles.held: The Apex Court has held that technicality should not be allowed to stand in the way of quashing criminal proceeding.
cited_cases: Shiji @ Pappu and Ors. Vs. Radhika and another, (2011) CJ (SC) 239

legal_principles.principle: Courts should accept the terms of a compromise even in criminal proceedings where the question involved is of a purely personal nature.
legal_principles.held: This Court summed up the approach to be adopted in such cases in the following words: 'We need to emphasise that it is perhaps advisable that in disputes where the question involved is of a purely personal nature, the court should ordinarily accept the terms of the compromise even in criminal proceedings...'

legal_principles.principle: The court should not allow technicalities to stand in the way of quashing criminal proceedings where there is a genuine settlement between parties.
legal_principles.held: This Court summed up the approach to be adopted in such cases in the following words: 'We need to emphasise that it is perhaps advisable that in disputes where the question involved is of a purely personal nature, the court should ordinarily accept the terms of the compromise even in criminal proceedings...'

outcome.final_order: The Court has inherent jurisdiction to pass a suitable order as may be necessary to prevent the abuse of process of law to secure the ends of justice.
